conventions: TypeScript, formatted by the repo Prettier config (@backstage/cli/config/prettier): single quotes, trailing commas, 2-space indent, 80-column wrap, arrow parens avoided for single params (x => x).

Every file in this change already exists except the changeset; never touch the Apache 2.0 header or its year in an existing file. A new .ts/.tsx file would need the header with year 2026, but this change adds none.

Match the file being edited: in plugins/scaffolder-react/src/next, arrow-function const exports for helpers and hooks, plain function declarations where the file already uses them (ReviewState/util.ts), JsonObject/JsonValue from @backstage/types with local isObject/isJsonObject type guards.

Imports: keep each file's existing import order and only add names to existing import statements or add one new import line where a site says so; no new npm dependencies (reuse lodash, json-schema-library, @rjsf/*).
No public API change: do not add anything to plugins/scaffolder-react/src/next/lib/index.ts, hooks/index.ts, components/index.ts or any barrel, and do not edit report*.api.md.

Tests run on Jest through backstage-cli (describe/it, expect matchers, jest.fn). Prefer fewer, thorough tests with several assertions each. In React Testing Library tests use screen and findBy*/queryBy* queries, not waitFor, and add no test IDs to implementation code.

Stepper tests render with renderInTestApp from @backstage/test-utils inside <SecretsContextProvider>, and wrap clicks that submit a step (Next, Review, Back, Create) in await act(async () => { fireEvent.click(...) }) exactly as the existing Stepper tests do.

Docs follow docs/contribute/doc-style-guide.md: U.S. English, second person, bold for UI elements, code style for keywords and parameter names, fenced code blocks tagged yaml, Prettier-formatted Markdown.
Changesets: add a new file only, never edit an existing .changeset file, never use the changeset CLI; write for adopters in plain language with no function, class or variable names.
Never run yarn build, yarn changesets version or yarn release.

decisions.topic: How a step's dependencies on an earlier-step answer reach the form
decisions.choice: At parse time in useTemplateSchema, a new pure helper liftCrossStepDependencies in lib/schema.ts rewrites each dependencies entry whose trigger key is not in the step's own properties into an equivalent allOf if/then entry; the rewritten schema feeds both mergedSchema and extractSchemaFromStep.
rejected: Injecting hidden stub properties for earlier-step keys into the step schema
Resolving every condition ourselves with retrieveSchema before handing the schema to rjsf
Changing Stepper.tsx to pass a merged multi-step schema to the Form
decisions.reason: rjsf skips a dependency whose trigger is not in the step's properties, while if/then is already evaluated against the whole formData (stepsState); lifting only those skipped entries fixes cross-step dependencies without changing same-step behaviour.

decisions.choice: Only entries where the step schema has a properties object and the dependency key is not an own key of it; steps without properties, same-step dependencies and boolean dependency values stay untouched.
rejected: Lift only when the key is defined in an earlier step
decisions.reason: This is exactly the set rjsf silently skips today, so no template that works today changes, and the existing useTemplateSchema test for a step with dependencies and no properties keeps passing.

decisions.choice: Array dependency D on key k becomes {if: {required: [k]}, then: {required: D}}; schema dependency S without oneOf becomes {if: {required: [k]}, then: S}; schema dependency with oneOf becomes one {if: {properties: {k: branch.properties[k]}, required: [k]}, then: branch without properties[k]} per branch that defines properties[k], plus {if: {required: [k]}, then: rest} when the dependency has keys besides oneOf.
decisions.reason: Matches rjsf and JSON Schema dependency semantics (applies when the trigger has an answer; a oneOf branch applies when its trigger subschema matches) using keywords both rjsf and json-schema-library already resolve against data.

decisions.choice: No change to Stepper.tsx, createAsyncValidators.ts, Workflow or any file in plugins/scaffolder.
decisions.reason: The Form already receives formData={stepsState} and handleNext validates the full submitted formData, so with the lifted schema both rjsf and createAsyncValidators resolve conditions against all earlier answers; TemplateWizardPage and TemplateEditorForm render the shared Workflow/Stepper (FR-10).

decisions.choice: findSchemaForKey resolves each step's mergedSchema with getSchema against the full form state minus the looked-up key; a key found in no step but declared in some step's conditional branch (isKeyDeclaredInSchemas) is dropped from Review; a key declared nowhere is still listed under formatKey(key).
rejected: Keep passing only the dependency keys as data
Pass the full form state including the key
decisions.reason: Removing the key itself stops json-schema-library from inventing a schema from the value, while every other answer (same step or earlier step) drives if/then/else, allOf and dependencies, so active branch fields get their title and review options and inactive ones disappear.

decisions.topic: Values of fields whose condition stopped holding
decisions.choice: Dropped from the Review step only; onCreate still receives them unchanged.
decisions.reason: Resolved at Gate 1 to the default; keeps the change narrow and does not alter what existing templates submit.
